record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the smallest repetition exponent that can still be avoided by an infinite word produced by iterated prefix-suffix duplication?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum exponent of a repetition which is avoidable by an infinite word constructed by iterated (prefix)-suffix dupli- cation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. The prefix duplication operation on a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ produces, from $w = uv$ with $u$ a nonempty prefix, the word $uuv$; the suffix duplication operation produces, from $w = uv$ with $v$ a nonempty suffix, the word $uvv$. A (finite or infinite) word $z$ is said to be obtained by iterated prefix-suffix duplication starting from a word $w_0$ if there is a (possibly infinite) sequence $w_0, w_1, w_2, \dots$ such that each $w_{i+1}$ is obtained from $w_i$ by a single prefix duplication or suffix duplication, and $z$ is the limit (or a member) of this sequence.

For a real number $\alpha > 1$, an $\alpha$-repetition (or repetition of exponent $\alpha$) in an infinite word is a nonempty factor of the form $u^k u'$ where $u'$ is a prefix of $u$ and $(k|u| + |u'|)/|u| \ge \alpha$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w}$ avoids exponent $\alpha$ (is $\alpha$-free) if it contains no factor of exponent $\ge \alpha$.

Determine the infimum of all real numbers $\alpha > 1$ such that there exists an infinite word, over some finite alphabet, that is obtained by iterated prefix-suffix duplication from some finite seed word and avoids exponent $\alpha$ (equivalently, contains no repetition of exponent $\ge \alpha$).
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface the body of work on prefix-suffix duplication and prefix-suffix square completion (including results that infinite words generated by such operations can avoid exponents greater than 2 in some related settings), but no source clearly determines the exact minimum avoidable repetition exponent for infinite words generated by iterated prefix-suffix duplication. The status of this specific question appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix duplication - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: A bio-inspired operation duplicating a prefix or a suffix of a word; language-theoretic results are given but the optimal avoidable repetition exponent for iterated prefix-suffix duplication is not pinned down.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on iterated prefix-suffix duplication exist, without resolving the minimum avoidable exponent.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses square completion variants and avoidance of higher-exponent repetitions, but for the related square-completion operation rather than answering the duplication question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses repetition avoidance for the square completion variant, not the exact minimum exponent for iterated prefix-suffix duplication.
